disclaimer: Informational only - amounts and eligibility vary by person, school, employer, and year, and programs change. VetPath does not determine eligibility. Confirm every program at its official source before counting on it.

programs.name: Post-9/11 GI Bill
programs.amount: Full in-state public tuition (or up to the yearly private/out-of-state cap), a monthly housing allowance, and up to $1,000/yr for books.
programs.eligibility: Amount is tied to your qualifying active-duty time - 100% at 36+ months of service.
programs.stackNote: The base most funded paths build on.
programs.tip: See your exact housing allowance in VA's GI Bill Comparison Tool.

programs.name: VR&E (Chapter 31)
programs.amount: Pays tuition and required fees in full, plus a monthly subsistence allowance while you train.
programs.eligibility: For a service-connected disability with an employment need - often fuller coverage than the GI Bill. You generally use one or the other for a given program.
programs.stackNote: The disability track - usually the strongest option if you qualify.

programs.name: Yellow Ribbon Program
programs.amount: Covers tuition above the GI Bill's cap - the school pledges an amount and VA matches it dollar-for-dollar.
programs.eligibility: For veterans at the 100% Post-9/11 tier, at participating schools. Not combined with VR&E.
programs.stackNote: Closes the gap at private, graduate, and out-of-state programs.

programs.name: VET TEC (high-tech training)
programs.amount: Covers tuition for approved coding, IT, data, and cybersecurity programs plus a monthly housing stipend - without using your GI Bill entitlement.
programs.eligibility: For VA-approved tech programs. Availability is limited and program-specific - confirm current status with VA.
programs.stackNote: A tech on-ramp that saves your GI Bill for later.

programs.name: Pat Tillman Foundation
programs.amount: Scholarship funding plus a national leadership network for veterans, service members, and military spouses.
programs.stackNote: Stacks on top of your federal benefits.

programs.name: Student Veterans of America
programs.amount: Dozens of scholarships for student veterans, funded by SVA and corporate partners.
programs.eligibility: For enrolled or enrolling student veterans - apply directly.
programs.stackNote: Field- and background-specific awards you can stack on top.

programs.name: Aviation & aerospace scholarships (OBAP)
programs.amount: Scholarships toward pilot training and aerospace careers.
programs.eligibility: For students pursuing aviation/aerospace - apply directly. An example of a field- and background-specific award you can stack on federal benefits.
programs.stackNote: Field-specific money on top of the GI Bill.

programs.name: Employer-paid tuition
programs.amount: Big employers pre-pay school - Amazon Career Choice, Walmart's Live Better U ($1/day college), and Starbucks' College Achievement Plan (100% tuition), among others.
programs.eligibility: Often a perk from day one, even part-time. Confirm the terms with the employer.
programs.stackNote: Let the job fund your next degree - and save your GI Bill.

programs.name: DoD SkillBridge
programs.amount: Train or intern with a civilian employer during your last up-to-180 days of service - while you keep full military pay and benefits.
programs.eligibility: For service members within ~180 days of separation, with command approval.
programs.stackNote: Get hired before you take off the uniform.

programs.name: Veterans' hiring preference + incentives
programs.amount: Veterans' Preference gives you an edge in federal hiring, and hard-to-fill roles can add recruitment, relocation, or retention incentives (commonly up to 25% of salary).
programs.eligibility: For federal employment - preference eligibility depends on your service. VRA lets agencies hire eligible veterans directly.
programs.stackNote: A faster lane into stable federal careers.

programs.name: Public Service Loan Forgiveness
programs.amount: Forgives your entire remaining federal student-loan balance after 120 qualifying monthly payments (about 10 years).
programs.eligibility: For full-time work with government or a nonprofit - including many healthcare, teaching, and public-safety jobs.
programs.stackNote: Turns a public-service career into loan freedom.

programs.name: Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert)
programs.amount: Certifies your business as veteran-owned (VOSB) or service-disabled-veteran-owned (SDVOSB) - unlocking federal contract set-asides reserved for those businesses.
programs.eligibility: Business must be at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more veterans (SDVOSB requires a service-connected disability). Free to apply.
programs.stackNote: For most veteran owners, certification is worth more than any grant.

programs.name: Women-Owned Small Business certification (WOSB / EDWOSB)
programs.amount: Qualifies your business for federal contracts set aside for women-owned small businesses in eligible industries.
programs.eligibility: Business at least 51% owned and controlled by women who are U.S. citizens; EDWOSB adds economic-disadvantage criteria. Stacks with VetCert - a woman veteran can hold both.
programs.stackNote: The women-owned set-aside lane - holds alongside the veteran one.

programs.name: Boots to Business
programs.amount: Free two-day entrepreneurship intro plus follow-on courses - the TAP entrepreneurship track.
programs.eligibility: Transitioning service members and spouses; a Reboot version serves veterans already out.
programs.stackNote: The free classroom before you spend a dollar.

programs.name: Veteran business support (OVBD & VBOCs)
programs.amount: Free one-on-one counseling, training, and plan reviews through SBA's veteran business network.
programs.eligibility: Veterans, service members, and military spouses at any stage - idea to expansion.
programs.stackNote: A free advisor who has walked other veterans through this exact path.

programs.name: Women's Business Centers
programs.amount: Free and low-cost training, counseling, and access-to-capital help at 100+ centers nationwide.
programs.eligibility: Open to women entrepreneurs at every stage.
programs.stackNote: The women-focused arm of the same free SBA network.

programs.name: V-WISE
programs.amount: Entrepreneurship training program for women veterans and military spouses - online phase, in-person residency, and ongoing support.
programs.eligibility: Women veterans, active-duty women, and women military spouses/partners.
programs.stackNote: Built specifically for women who served.

programs.name: Grants.gov
programs.amount: The official database of every federal grant - the place to check what actually exists for your industry and situation.
programs.eligibility: Varies by grant. True small-business grants are rare and competitive - most federal support flows through contracts and certifications instead.
programs.tip: Never pay anyone for a 'grant list' - the real list is free, right here.
programs.stackNote: The honest answer to 'what grants exist' - straight from the source.
